meta.titre: Rate of Stock Turnover: measuring how fast stock is sold
meta.sous_theme: Average stock, cost of goods sold, rate of turnover and related profit figures

sections.contenu_markdown: A provision-shop owner in Bamenda notices that bags of rice leave her shelves within days, while some decorative curtains stay unsold for months. Money tied up in unsold goods cannot be used to buy new goods or to pay the rent. The rate of stock turnover tells a trader how many times the stock is sold and replaced in a period. The GCE Commerce papers ask for it together with gross profit, net profit and margin, so you must be able to go from opening and closing stock to every final figure.

items: Stock (inventory) is the goods a business holds for sale.
Purchases are the goods bought during the period, and sales are the goods sold.
Gross profit is sales minus the cost of the goods sold, and net profit is gross profit minus expenses.
A percentage is found by dividing by the whole and multiplying by 100.

sections.titre: Average stock and the rate of turnover
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Key terms
- **Opening stock**: the value of stock at the start of the trading period. **Closing stock**: the value of stock left at the end.
- **Average stock** $= \dfrac{\text{Opening stock} + \text{Closing stock}}{2}$
- **Cost of goods sold (COGS)** $= \text{Opening stock} + \text{Purchases} - \text{Closing stock}$ (add carriage inwards to purchases when it is given).
- **Sales** is the value of goods sold at selling prices. A question may call it **turnover**.

### Formulas
$$\text{Rate of stock turnover} = \frac{\text{Cost of goods sold}}{\text{Average stock}} \ \text{(times per period)}$$

$$\text{Gross profit} = \text{Sales} - \text{COGS} \qquad \text{Net profit} = \text{Gross profit} - \text{Expenses}$$

$$\text{Margin} = \frac{\text{Gross profit}}{\text{Sales}} \times 100\% \qquad \text{Net profit as a \% of sales} = \frac{\text{Net profit}}{\text{Sales}} \times 100\%$$

The rate of turnover is a **number of times**, not an amount of money. Both COGS and average stock are valued at **cost price**, which is why sales are never used in the rate.

### What the rate tells a trader
- A **high rate** means stock sells quickly: little money is tied up, storage costs are low and goods are less likely to spoil or go out of fashion. A rate that is too high can mean the shop often runs out of goods and loses customers.
- A **low rate** means slow selling, overstocking, higher storage costs and a greater risk of damaged or unsold goods.
- A trader can raise the rate by running promotions, ordering smaller quantities more often and stocking what customers really ask for.

variantes.nom: Cost of goods sold is not given
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a table gives sales (turnover) and gross profit but no purchases or stocks.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use $\text{COGS} = \text{Sales} - \text{Gross profit}$. For example, sales of 500,000 FCFA and gross profit of 125,000 FCFA give COGS of 375,000 FCFA. Then divide by the average stock.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how long stock stays in the business.
variantes.contenu_markdown: $\text{Days to sell the stock} = \dfrac{\text{Number of days in the period}}{\text{Rate of turnover}}$. A rate of 4 over a 360-day year or a 365-day year means the average stock is sold about every 90 or 91 days. Use the number of days the question gives.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the rate and the COGS are given and a stock value is missing.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Rearrange: $\text{Average stock} = \dfrac{\text{COGS}}{\text{Rate}}$. Then $\text{Closing stock} = 2 \times \text{Average stock} - \text{Opening stock}$, because the average is half of the sum of the two stocks.

sections.enonce_markdown: A trader in Bafoussam gives these figures for one year: opening stock 300,000 FCFA, purchases 1,500,000 FCFA, closing stock 200,000 FCFA, sales 2,200,000 FCFA and working expenses 150,000 FCFA. Calculate (a) the cost of goods sold, (b) the average stock, (c) the rate of stock turnover, (d) the gross profit, (e) the margin, correct to one decimal place, and (f) the net profit.

etapes.action: Calculate the cost of goods sold
etapes.justification: COGS = opening stock + purchases - closing stock.
Average stock is half of the sum of opening and closing stock.

etapes.action: Calculate the rate of stock turnover
etapes.justification: Rate = COGS divided by average stock, both at cost price.
Margin is gross profit as a percentage of sales.

sections.conclusion_markdown: COGS is 1,600,000 FCFA, average stock 250,000 FCFA, rate of turnover 6.4 times, gross profit 600,000 FCFA, margin 27.3% and net profit 450,000 FCFA. The stock is sold and replaced 6.4 times during the year.

items.pourquoi_faux: Sales are at selling price while stock is valued at cost price, so the two cannot be compared. The rate uses the cost of goods sold.
The goods still in the shop at the end of the period were not sold, so their value must be taken out.
The average of two numbers is found by adding them and dividing by 2, not by subtracting.

items.erreur_markdown: The rate of stock turnover is 6.4 FCFA.
items.pourquoi_faux: The rate says how many times the stock is sold and replaced, so it is a number of times and has no currency unit.
items.correction_markdown: The rate of stock turnover is 6.4 times a year.

items.erreur_markdown: A trader with a very low rate of turnover says the business is doing very well because it keeps a large stock.
items.pourquoi_faux: A low rate means stock is slow to sell. Money is tied up in goods, storage costs rise and goods may spoil or become out of date.
items.correction_markdown: A low rate is a warning sign. The trader should hold less stock or promote the slow goods.

items.enonce_markdown: A shop sold goods which had cost 900,000 FCFA to buy during the year. Its opening stock was 140,000 FCFA and its closing stock was 160,000 FCFA. Calculate the average stock and the rate of stock turnover.
items.solution_markdown:
Average stock $= \frac{140\,000 + 160\,000}{2} = 150\,000$ FCFA.
Rate of turnover $= \frac{900\,000}{150\,000} = 6$ times.
**Average stock 150,000 FCFA; rate of turnover 6 times.**

items.enonce_markdown: A trader's accounts for the year show: opening stock 80,000 FCFA, closing stock 120,000 FCFA, purchases 740,000 FCFA, sales 910,000 FCFA and working expenses 95,000 FCFA. Calculate (a) the cost of goods sold, (b) the rate of stock turnover, (c) the gross profit, (d) the net profit and (e) the net profit as a percentage of sales, correct to one decimal place.

Two shops, P and Q, sell the same kind of goods. Shop P has sales of 3,600,000 FCFA, average stock of 400,000 FCFA and gross profit of 1,200,000 FCFA. Shop Q has sales of 3,000,000 FCFA, average stock of 750,000 FCFA and gross profit of 1,200,000 FCFA. (a) Calculate the rate of stock turnover of each shop. (b) Calculate the margin of each shop, correct to one decimal place. (c) State which shop uses its stock more efficiently and which earns more on each 100 FCFA of sales. (d) Shop Q had an opening stock of 800,000 FCFA and wants a rate of 3 next year with the same COGS. Calculate the average stock it needs and the closing stock that would give it.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) COGS of P $= 3\,600\,000 - 1\,200\,000 = 2\,400\,000$ FCFA, so its rate $= \frac{2\,400\,000}{400\,000} = 6$ times.
COGS of Q $= 3\,000\,000 - 1\,200\,000 = 1\,800\,000$ FCFA, so its rate $= \frac{1\,800\,000}{750\,000} = 2.4$ times.
(b) Margin of P $= \frac{1\,200\,000}{3\,600\,000} \times 100\% = 33.3\%$. Margin of Q $= \frac{1\,200\,000}{3\,000\,000} \times 100\% = 40\%$.
(c) Shop P uses its stock more efficiently (6 times against 2.4 times). Shop Q earns more on each 100 FCFA of sales (40 FCFA against about 33.3 FCFA), but its stock stays in the shop much longer.
(d) Average stock needed $= \frac{1\,800\,000}{3} = 600\,000$ FCFA. Closing stock $= 2 \times 600\,000 - 800\,000 = 400\,000$ FCFA.
**P 6 times, Q 2.4 times; margins 33.3% and 40%; average stock 600,000 FCFA; closing stock 400,000 FCFA.**

items_markdown: Rate of stock turnover = cost of goods sold divided by average stock, and it is a number of times in the period.
Average stock = (opening stock + closing stock) divided by 2; COGS = opening stock + purchases - closing stock.
When COGS is not given, use sales minus gross profit.
A high rate shows fast-selling stock and less money tied up; a very low rate shows overstocking and a risk of spoilage.
After the rate, gross profit = sales - COGS, net profit = gross profit - expenses, and margin = gross profit / sales x 100%.
